title: Look up a member's regular savings balance
description: Given a member number, searches the servicing console and returns the member's Regular Savings account balance. Returns a business outcome (not an error) if the member number does not exist or the operator is not entitled to view the record.
goal: look up member 12345 and read their regular savings balance

params.name: member_id
params.description: The member number to search for.

outputs.name: regular_savings_balance
outputs.description: The member's Regular Savings account balance, as displayed (e.g. '4,182.55').

locator.name: Regular Savings Balance:

fallbacks.weaker_because: Falls back to substring-matching any node whose name contains this text, ignoring role and ordinal entirely -- used only if the primary role+name+ordinal match misses, e.g. after a markup change that adds an extra cell to the row.

locator.rationale: The value half of a label:value table-cell pair (see keystone/surface/web.py's pairing heuristic): its accessible name is inherited from the caption cell physically to its left ('Regular Savings Balance:'), and its own text is exposed separately as AXNode.value. Because the label half of the pair is deliberately excluded from perception, this is the only 'cell' node with this name, so ordinal 0 is correct and not a smell here -- verified live: two candidate nodes existed before that exclusion was added, and the label (not the value) landed at ordinal 0, which silently returned the caption instead of the balance. Scoped to the top-level document (frame_path is empty) because the entry URL is the lookup page loaded directly, not through the tenant frameset.

target.name: Member #:

fallbacks.weaker_because: Structural selector tied to this specific HTML attribute name rather than rendered meaning; a vendor markup change that renames the field's `name` attribute (but keeps the caption) would break this fallback while the primary accessible-name match keeps working.

target.rationale: The field carries no <label for> anywhere in this app -- its caption is the table cell physically to its left ('Member #:'), which is exactly the adjacent-cell heuristic keystone/surface/web.py's accessible-name computation implements. Harbor Point renames this same field's caption to 'Account Number:' and reorders it in the form; a per-tenant TenantOverride patches the name for that tenant, but the reorder itself requires no change at all, since targeting is by name, not position.

locator.name: Member #:
locator.rationale: Same field as the step target; re-resolved rather than reusing a live reference, per the ref/locator distinction -- the checkpoint asserts against the surface exactly as replay would months later.

checkpoint.description: the member field visibly holds the value we just typed

steps.note: The member field has no accessible name of its own in markup; it is targeted by the adjacent-left table cell's caption.

target.name: Search
target.rationale: Named directly by its own `value` attribute (a submit input), the second-highest-priority step in the accessible-name computation -- this is the strongest kind of targeting available. frame_path is empty because the lookup page is loaded directly rather than through the tenant frameset, where a same-named 'Search' link also exists in the nav frame; that link is a distinct node scoped to a different frame_path and would never be confused with this one even in the frameset case.

locator.name: Regular Savings Balance:
locator.rationale: Same locator as the output extraction below. Its presence after clicking Search is exactly the condition that distinguishes 'we landed on a member record' from the two business outcomes and from a hard failure -- all three land on a URL matching the same /member/:id route, so the checkpoint has to look at content, not the URL.

checkpoint.description: the member summary panel (with a Regular Savings Balance row) is showing

steps.note: Search is classified safe by policy.yaml -- it is a read-only lookup, not a posting action.

target.name: Regular Savings Balance:
target.rationale: See the output's rationale above -- identical locator, since this step and the output extraction read the same value. The step's read is part of the recorded flow (and would feed a later step via ValueSource(kind='extracted') in a more complex capability); the output extraction re-resolves and re-reads independently at the end, per design rule 6, rather than trusting this step's captured value.

steps.note: No checkpoint on this step: step 1's checkpoint already established the value is present before this read is attempted.

locator.name: Regular Savings Balance:
locator.rationale: Independent re-assertion of the flow's overall goal, evaluated against the live surface rather than inferred from 'every step reported ok' -- design rule 6.

success.description: the Regular Savings Balance was displayed for this member

business_outcomes.description: No member exists with the given number. A legitimate host answer, not an error.

locator.name: NO RECORD FOUND
locator.rationale: The host's not-found message includes the searched member number ('NO RECORD FOUND FOR MEMBER 99999'), which varies per call, so the locator matches on the fixed leading substring rather than the full text. role=status is how this app marks a host response message, distinguishing it from role=alert (used for authorisation failures) purely by role -- no text-scraping needed to tell the two business outcomes apart.

business_outcomes.description: The record exists but this operator is not entitled to view it. A legitimate host answer, not an error.

locator.name: NOT ENTITLED
locator.rationale: role=alert (not role=status) is how this app marks an authorisation failure; matched on a fixed substring of the message for the same reason as MEMBER_NOT_FOUND above.

recoveries.description: A message-of-the-day dialog covers the page on load and must be dismissed before any control underneath it is interactable.

locator.name: System Message
locator.rationale: Named explicitly via aria-label in this app's markup ('System Message'), the highest-priority source in the accessible-name computation -- no adjacent-cell heuristic needed here.

target.name: Continue
target.rationale: Named by its own `value` attribute, same as the Search button.

escalations.description: The session expired mid-flow and the app redirected to its sign-in screen.

detect.description: the app bounced to the sign-in screen

escalations.guidance: Re-authenticate in this live session, then resume -- automation cannot do this itself: policy.yaml explicitly denies the signin route to the agent, so there is no automated path through this state by design, not an oversight.

0.name: Account Number:
0.rationale: Harbor Point renames this field's caption from 'Member #:' to 'Account Number:'. The field's reordering within the form (branch first, then this field) needs no override at all -- accessible-name targeting is positionless by construction; only the caption rename requires patching.

1.name: Find
1.rationale: Harbor Point also renames the submit button's caption from 'Search' to 'Find' (mockapp/data.py's per-tenant search_button config) -- a second, independent caption difference from the field rename above, not a variant of it. Confirmed live against the mock during Phase 1 (dump_ax.py showed button "Find" on harbor's lookup page) before this override was written.

tenant_overrides.note: Same product (v7.2) as pinnacle; two static per-tenant caption differences (the searched field's label and the submit button's label), each patched independently. Still a small, reviewable diff, not a re-recording -- see TenantOverride's own docstring on what a large override count would signal. See BUILD_PLAN.md's cross-tenant stretch goal.
